default.notes: A stamped visa (visa estampada) from a Panamanian consulate is required. Holders of a valid, already-used US, Canadian, UK, Australian or Schengen visa can normally enter for 30 days without one.

groups.notes: Visa-free for tourism, normally 90 days on arrival — some nationalities have been granted up to 180. The officer sets the days, so check your entry record and extend through the Servicio Nacional de Migración if needed.

Restricted nationality — an authorised visa (visa autorizada) must be cleared in advance by Panama's National Immigration Service, normally with a sponsor in Panama. Allow one to three months, and note that the third-country visa waiver does not apply.

PA.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Panamanian citizens.

CO.notes: Colombian citizens need a stamped visa despite the shared border, but a valid and already-used US, Canadian, UK, Australian or Schengen visa normally allows visa-free entry for 30 days instead.

VE.notes: Panama reimposed a visa requirement on Venezuelan citizens in 2017. A stamped consular visa is needed; the third-country visa waiver is applied inconsistently, so confirm with the consulate.

DO.notes: Dominican citizens need a stamped consular visa, though holders of a used US, Canadian, UK, Australian or Schengen visa can normally enter visa-free for 30 days.

CN.notes: Chinese citizens need a stamped consular visa. In practice most travellers use the third-country waiver with a valid, already-used US or Schengen visa — confirm current terms with the consulate.

IN.notes: Indian citizens need a stamped consular visa, but a valid and already-used US, Canadian, UK, Australian or Schengen visa normally permits visa-free entry for 30 days.

TW.notes: Panama switched recognition from Taipei to Beijing in 2017 and the Taiwanese embassy closed; Taiwanese passport holders should expect to need a consular visa. Confirm the current position before booking.

XK.notes: Kosovan passports are not on Panama's visa-exempt list — apply for a stamped consular visa, or use the third-country visa waiver if you hold a qualifying US or Schengen visa.
